# Destination capabilities

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:capabilities` from src/connectors/destinations/kind-registry.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

What each destination can do in Noti today, generated from the destination registry (spec 09 F105 and
F120, ADR 0052). It describes what Noti’s adapter for each mode does, not everything the provider
could do: Discord can edit a message, for example, but Noti does not keep message ids yet, so it says
No. Provider facts cite the section of [`DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md`](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md)
they come from (researched 2026-10-13). Where that reference does not state a value, this page says so.

This page is documentation, not acceptance evidence: nothing on it shows that a real provider account
accepted a Noti message.

## Capability matrix

| | Lark | Slack | Microsoft Teams | Discord | Custom webhook |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mode | `custom_bot` | `incoming_webhook` | `workflows_webhook` | `incoming_webhook` | `signed_https` |
| Availability | Offered | Offered | Offered | Offered | Off unless `GENERIC_WEBHOOK_ENABLED=true` (deployment flag) |
| Message formats, richest first | card, markdown, plain | card, markdown, plain | card, markdown, plain | card, markdown, plain | card |
| What a success means | Delivered: `code: 0` in the response body (§3.1) | Delivered: HTTP 200 with the body `ok` (§1.2) | **Accepted only**: HTTP 202, and the flow can still fail afterwards (§2.2) | Delivered: the created message is returned, because Noti always sends `wait=true` (§4) | A 2xx from the customer endpoint; a 202 is shown as accepted, not delivered |
| Request signed | Yes, Lark HMAC-SHA256 (with the secret from Lark) | No | No | No | Yes, Standard Webhooks v1 (secret generated by Noti, shown once) |
| Links back to the source | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| @mentions | No: untrusted text never pings anyone | No: untrusted text never pings anyone | No: untrusted text never pings anyone | No: untrusted text never pings anyone | No: untrusted text never pings anyone |
| Update a sent message | No | No | No | No | No |
| Delete a sent message | No | No | No | No | No |
| Reply in a thread | No | No | No | No | No |
| Interactive buttons | No | No | No | No | No |
| Custom sender name or icon | No | No | No | No | No |
| Server-side deduplication | No: a retry can appear twice | No: a retry can appear twice | No: a retry can appear twice | No: a retry can appear twice | No: a retry can appear twice |
| Phone numbers and emails masked | Yes | No | No | No | No |
| Body budget | 20,000 bytes | 40,000 bytes | 28,000 bytes | 40,000 bytes | 64,000 bytes |
| Title limit | 200 characters | 150 characters | 200 characters | 256 characters | 500 characters |
| Text limit | 3,000 characters | 3,000 characters | 3,000 characters | 4,096 characters | 4,096 characters |
| Credential | A URL the customer supplies, stored encrypted and never shown again | A URL the customer supplies, stored encrypted and never shown again | A URL the customer supplies, stored encrypted and never shown again | A URL the customer supplies, stored encrypted and never shown again | A URL the customer supplies, stored encrypted and never shown again |

The adapters read these values from the registry at render time, and `tests/destinations/conformance.test.ts`
pins them in a golden table. When a message is too large for one format, Noti tries the next in the list.
An over-long field is shortened visibly with an ellipsis; a message that fits no format fails as
`payload_too_large` rather than being cut off silently.

## Limits and where they come from

“Noti budget” is a limit Noti sets where the provider has none. “Not stated” means Noti enforces a value
the reference does not give; it is listed so it can be checked, not hidden.

### Lark

| Limit | Value | Basis | Source | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Request body | 20,000 bytes | Provider | [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §3.1](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “请求体的数据大小不能超过 **20 KB**” | Read as decimal kilobytes, the conservative reading. Enforced as `maxBodyBytes`. |
| Card title | 200 characters | Noti budget | not stated | Noti readability limit. The reference states no title limit. Enforced as `maxTitleChars`. |
| Card text | 3,000 characters | Noti budget | not stated | Noti readability limit. The reference states no text limit. Enforced as `maxTextChars`. |
| Rate limit per custom bot | 100 per minute, 5 per second | Provider | [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §3.1](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “100 次/分钟，5 次/秒” |  |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Enforced as `maxBodyBytes`. |
| Section text | 3,000 characters | Provider | [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §1.6](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “1–**3000** chars” | Enforced as `maxTextChars`. |

| Blocks per message | 50 | Provider | [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §1.6](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “Blocks per message \| **50**” |  |

| Message size | 28,000 bytes | Provider | [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §2.2](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “"**approximately 28 KB**. This limit includes all HTML elements” | Read as decimal kilobytes, the conservative reading. Enforced as `maxBodyBytes`. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Request body budget | 64,000 bytes | Noti budget | not stated | Noti budget: the customer owns the endpoint, so there is no provider limit. Enforced as `maxBodyBytes`. |

## What is not known

- **Lark.** The complete Lark error-code table could not be loaded; unknown codes are expected. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §3.5](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “Unresolved: the full Lark error-code table”
- **Slack.** Slack documents no server-side idempotency for incoming webhooks, so a retried delivery can appear twice. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §1.2](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “**Idempotency:** none.”
- **Microsoft Teams.** A 202 from the Workflows trigger is acceptance, not delivery: the flow can still fail afterwards. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §2.2](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “This is acknowledge-on-receive, *not*”
- **Microsoft Teams.** Power Automate and Logic Apps throttling numbers were not retrieved. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §2.2](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “GAP — Power Automate / Logic Apps request throttling”
- **Microsoft Teams.** Delivery to private channels is unproven: two official Microsoft sources disagree. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §2.2](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “CONFLICT — private channels”
- **Microsoft Teams.** The maximum Adaptive Card version Teams supports is not published. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §8](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “maximum supported Adaptive Card `version` for Teams”
- **Discord.** The per-route numeric limit for Execute Webhook is not documented in a form that could be read. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §4](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “UNVERIFIED — per-route numeric limit for `Execute Webhook`”

## Features checked when a destination is saved

The integrations API refuses a requested `format` or `features` entry that the destination cannot
provide, with the reason, instead of storing it and silently doing less at delivery (spec 07 F93).
Only the default (richest) format can be named today, because no stored setting holds a format choice.

| Feature (`features` value) | Lark | Slack | Microsoft Teams | Discord | Custom webhook |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| updating a message in place (`update_in_place`) | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported |
| deleting a sent message (`delete_message`) | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported |
| replying in a thread (`thread_replies`) | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported |
| interactive buttons (`interactive_buttons`) | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported |
| @mentions (`mentions`) | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported |
| a custom sender name or icon (`custom_identity`) | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported | Refused: not supported |

## Not offered

- **Telegram.** A bot token belongs to one bot owner, so there is no way for a customer to grant a multi-tenant service scoped access (spec 09 F110). [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §5](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “Telegram has **no OAuth and no multi-tenant app concept**”
- **Microsoft Teams Office 365 Connectors.** Retired by Microsoft. Teams is offered through Workflows only. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §2.1](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “**Microsoft 365 / Office 365 Connectors were permanently disabled on 18–22 May 2026.**”
- **Email.** Not built. The sending quota and the third-party provider specifics are open questions. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §8](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “Cloudflare Email Sending daily quota number”
- **Slack Web API, Teams bot and Lark app modes.** Not built. Their capabilities differ materially from the webhook modes above (message update, threads, and for the Lark app server-side deduplication), so each gets its own registry entry when it ships. [DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md §7](DESTINATION_API_REFERENCE.md): “\| Server-side dedup \| ❌ \| ❌ \| ❌ \| ❌ \| ❌ \| ✅ `uuid` \|”
